v.3: We sent it down on a blessed night, and We have been warning [mankind].
v.4: Every definitive matter is resolved on it,
v.5: as an ordinance from Us. We have been sending [apostles]
v.6: as a mercy from your Lord—indeed He is the All-hearing, the All-knowing—
v.7: the Lord of the heavens and the earth, and whatever is between them, should you have conviction.
v.8: There is no god except Him: He gives life and brings death, your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers.
v.9: But they play around in doubt.
v.10: So watch out for the day when the sky brings on a manifest smoke,
v.11: enveloping the people. [They will cry out:] ‘This is a painful punishment.
v.12: Our Lord! Remove this punishment from us. Indeed we have believed!’
v.13: What will the admonition avail them, when a manifest apostle had already come to them,
v.14: but they turned away from him, and said, ‘A tutored madman?’
v.15: Indeed We will withdraw the punishment a little; but you will revert [to your earlier ways].
v.16: The day We shall strike with the most terrible striking, We will indeed take vengeance [on them].
v.17: Certainly We tried the people of Pharaoh before them, when a noble apostle came to them,
v.18: [saying,] ‘Give over the servants of Allah to me; indeed I am a trusted apostle [sent] to you.
v.19: Do not defy Allah. Indeed I bring you a manifest authority.
v.20: I seek the protection of my Lord and your Lord, lest you should stone me.
v.21: And if you do not believe me, keep out of my way.’
v.22: Then he invoked his Lord, [saying,] ‘These are indeed a guilty lot.’
v.23: [Allah told him,] ‘Set out by night with My servants; for you will be pursued.
v.24: Leave behind the sea unmoving; for they will be a drowned host.’
v.25: How many gardens and springs did they leave behind!
v.27: and the affluence wherein they rejoiced!
v.28: So it was; and We bequeathed them to another people.
v.29: So neither the sky wept for them, nor the earth; nor were they granted any respite.
v.30: Certainly We delivered the Children of Israel from the humiliating torment
v.31: of Pharaoh. Indeed, he was a tyrant among the transgressors.
v.32: Certainly We chose them knowingly above all the nations,
v.33: and We gave them some signs in which there was a manifest test.
v.35: ‘It will be only our first death, and we shall not be resurrected.
v.36: Bring our fathers back [to life], if you are truthful.’
v.37: Are they better, or the people of Tubba‘, and those who were before them? We destroyed them; indeed, they were guilty.
v.38: We did not create the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them for play.
v.39: We did not create them except with consummate wisdom; but most of them do not know.
v.40: Indeed the Day of Judgement is the tryst for them all,
v.41: the day when a friend will not avail a friend in any way, nor will they be helped,
v.42: except for him on whom Allah has mercy. Indeed He is the All-mighty, the All-merciful.
v.44: will be the food of the sinful.
v.45: Like molten copper it will boil in their bellies,
v.47: [The keepers of hell will be told,] ‘Seize him and drag him to the middle of hell,
v.48: then pour over his head boiling water as punishment,
v.49: [and tell them,] “Taste this! Indeed you are the [self-styled] mighty and noble!
v.50: This is what you used to doubt!’
v.51: Indeed the Godwary will be in a safe place,
v.53: dressed in fine silk and brocade, sitting face to face.
v.54: So shall it be, and We shall wed them to black-eyed houris.
v.55: Secure [from any kind of harm,] there they will call for every kind of fruit [they wish].
v.56: Other than the first death, they will not taste death therein, and He will save them from the punishment of hell
v.57: —a grace from your Lord. That is the great success.
v.58: Indeed We have made it simple in your language, so that they may take admonition.
